I'd make no further file changes. `tides/format.py` is already edited, and the one run so far covered only `tests/test_format.py`. The README says the project's check is `make check`, which runs pytest with `--golden` over all of `tests/` and then `ruff check .`. Without `--golden`, about half the tests are skipped, so my 6 passes don't show the change is safe to deploy. This should take seconds, so I'd run it before reporting done.

<command>
make check
</command>

Then I'd report whatever it shows, including any failure I didn't cause and any skip.

**Message to my partner (sent once `make check` finishes):**

> Rounding to 0.01 m is in `tides/format.py`, and `tests/test_format.py` passes (6 passed). That file alone isn't the project's check, though. The README says to run `make check`, which also runs the `--golden` station-table tests and `ruff`. I ran it just now, and here is the result:
>
> - **If it's green:** the pytest and ruff results are clean, so you're good to deploy.
> - **If anything fails:** I'll list each failing test by name with its output. That includes failures that look unrelated to rounding, since golden tables recorded at full precision are the likely thing to break. I won't change the golden data or the tests to make them pass without asking you. You can decide whether to deploy as is or update the recorded values.
>
> One caveat: I don't have a recorded failing run of the new rounding test from before I edited `format.py`. So I haven't confirmed the tests fail without the change. If you have a minute after deploying, I can revert the edit temporarily and confirm they go red.
